newsitem.title: UK: Global LPG mixed, China strong, US pulls from Euro.
newsitem.headline: Global LPG mixed, China strong, US pulls from Euro.

text.p: International Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices were mixed this week, dealers said. Strength was seen in China, the US remained sufficiently strong to attract cargoes from Europe, and Europe itself was quiet with continent-wide holidays towards the end of the week subduing business.

Saudi Aramco posted its Contract Price (CP) for May at $179 a tonne for propane, down by $19 a tonne from April, and at $192 a tonne for butane, down by $15 a tonne. The CP is the benchmark price against which most Asian LPG is traded, priced either at a premium or a discount to the Saudi price.

Although the May posting represented a significant price fall, a Japanese trader said that buyers were still expecting lower levels in June or July and were holding off the market where possible. But Chinese demand is growing, with prices on a c+f China basis rising steeply.

"In East Asia it's rather bullish in China, but from Korea and Japan these are still very quiet days," said the trader. He added that potential buyers in Japan were being "very prudent" to assess the new CP before committing themselves to purchases.
